s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of headache and vision loss with sinus inflammation
salient_findings: Severe headache with worsening over time
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
No history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
Recent diagnosis of COVID-19
Rhinorrhea three weeks prior to presentation
Headache for 2 weeks
Vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Severe pain on ocular motion
Right eye visual acuity limited to hand-motion detection
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation on CT
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone with extension of inflammation into the apex
Positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus
Elevated Serum IgG4 levels

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of headache and vision loss with sinus inflammation
salient_findings: Severe headache with worsening over time
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone

No history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
Recent diagnosis of COVID-19
Rhinorrhea three weeks prior to presentation
Headache for 2 weeks
Vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Severe pain on ocular motion
Right eye visual acuity limited to hand-motion detection

Elevated Serum IgG4 levels

shortlist.label: giant cell arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: temporal relationship with vision loss and headache

shortlist.label: sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation on CT

shortlist.label: optic neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: vision loss in the right eye for 2 days and severe pain on ocular motion

shortlist.label: pituitary apoplexy
shortlist.why_kept: acute onset of headache and vision loss

shortlist.label: sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: elevated Serum IgG4 levels and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells

raw.rationale: The patient's recent history of rhinorrhea, headache, and vision loss, combined with CT findings of opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and bony erosion, strongly support a diagnosis of sinusitis. The positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus further confirm this diagnosis.

rejected.label: giant cell arteritis
rejected.why: While the patient's age and headache could suggest giant cell arteritis, the presence of sinus opacification and positive sinus cultures point more strongly towards sinusitis.

rejected.label: optic neuritis
rejected.why: Optic neuritis could explain the vision loss, but it does not account for the sinus opacification and bony erosion seen on CT.

rejected.label: pituitary apoplexy
rejected.why: Pituitary apoplexy typically presents with sudden, severe headache and visual disturbances, but it does not explain the sinus findings.

rejected.label: sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis can cause sinusitis and elevated IgG4 levels, but the acute presentation and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus make sinusitis a more likely diagnosis.
